request_flow.summary: The developer invokes tools/newyou-local with dev or test and a child command. The wrapper checks the repository root, project declaration, supported DevCore version, and unresolved same-worktree jobs under an inheritable build lock. It then execs mise and DevCore run for the selected profile.

Before Repo startup, LocalConfig rejects partial markers, verifies the live managed job receipt, checks the exact slot and generation-derived database and role, validates environment binding, and rejects TEST partitions. Missing or mismatched managed context fails closed when the managed pool is declared.

Before local Dialyzer analysis, LocalDialyzer derives a cache identity from toolchain versions, Dialyxir source, the core application set, and core beam/application inputs. The cache helper serializes baseline preparation, checks its manifest and file hashes, publishes complete baselines atomically, and copies them to a distinct worktree-local directory before Dialyxir mutates them. The project PLT includes the already pinned Dialyxir API so the build task is analyzed without suppressing unknown-function findings.

Restart-child scripts invoke the existing read-only Proof.Result.capture_postgresql preflight before fixture operations. The production exclusion probe validates inherited TEST configuration while starting no Repo and keeping its private production build worktree-local. Actual managed subprocess execution remains unverified.

security_invariants.summary: Managed identity markers alone do not authorize a database target. LocalConfig requires a successful live DevCore receipt and exact field agreement. Verification failure, partial markers, stale allocation, mismatched worktree or database binding raises before Repo startup.
NewYou keeps shared DEV fixed at its legacy endpoint and identity. Managed jobs can select TEST only through the verified generation-specific TEST receipt. TEST partitioning remains unsupported.
The wrapper does not print captured DevCore status output or inherited credentials. Cache files and lock paths reject symlink substitution and unmanaged destination replacement.

The explicit ci compatibility mode preserves the runner-owned legacy allocation shape. Caller-controlled flags do not authenticate CI. The local entry point rejects this override and managed markers never fall back through it.

concurrency.summary: The command lock is scoped to a Git worktree and inherited by its child process chain. It excludes overlapping build commands in that worktree while permitting work in sibling worktrees. It does not lock TEST globally.

The PLT preparation lock is keyed to one cache identity and covers baseline validation or creation and atomic publication. The helper releases it before copying into a worktree path; Dialyzer analysis runs without holding the shared-cache lock, so separate worktrees use separate mutable PLT copies.

idempotency_retry.summary: A valid complete PLT baseline for the same cache key is reused. A failed producer does not publish an incomplete baseline, so a later attempt can prepare it again. A worktree copy with a matching ownership marker and cache key is reused.

failure_recovery.summary: Unavailable DevCore status, unsupported installation, unresolved same-worktree jobs, malformed project declaration, or unsafe lock state prevents child launch with a bounded non-secret diagnosis.

Invalid or incomplete PLT baseline metadata, digest mismatch, unsafe path, producer failure, or unowned destination prevents Dialyzer analysis. Staging files are removed on failed publication, and the previous owned local copy is restored when atomic replacement fails.

safe_extensions.summary: Keep DevCore receipt semantics and managed resource lifecycle in DevCore. NewYou should validate the returned identity and never duplicate slot allocation, generation advancement, credential provisioning, job supervision, or cleanup.
Add local command conveniences only through the managed entry point and preserve explicit legacy and CI compatibility gates.
Change PLT cache identity when the OTP, Elixir, Dialyxir source, core application set, core runtime inputs, or cache format changes. Continue to give each worktree its own writable PLT copies.

reuse.summary: Use the existing NewYou.Repo and runtime configuration seam for database target selection. No second Repo or business persistence path is introduced.
Use pinned Mix, OTP, Elixir, and Dialyxir tooling and preserve the existing GitHub Actions PLT cache behavior.

prohibited_shortcuts.summary: Do not infer authorization from a database name prefix, local environment markers, or a successful TCP connection without live DevCore receipt verification.
Do not partition the NOCREATEDB TEST role, fall back from managed mode to shared TEST, redirect managed work to DEV, or create NewYou-owned slot databases and roles.
Do not share mutable Dialyxir core PLT files across worktrees, hold the cache lock for full analysis, or serialize the TEST database and full test suite through the PLT lock.
